newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Cooperative Bank raises prime rate to 7.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Cooperative Bank raises prime rate to 7.4 pct.

text.p: State-owned Cooperative Bank of Taiwan, taking a cue from the Bank of Taiwan, said on Wednesday it was raising its prime lending rate by 0.125 percentage point to 7.4 percent, effective Thursday.
The bank also was raising its one-month-to-one-year time deposit rates by between 0.05 and 0.15 percentage point.
The rate hikes by the two state-owned commercial banks came nearly a week after the central bank's decision to increase two key interest rates to stabilise the foreign exchange market.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on July 31 the bank was raising the rediscount rate and accommodations against secured loans to 5.25 and 5.625 percent, respectively, effective August 1.
Bank of Taiwan, the island's biggest commercial bank, said on Wednesday it was raising its prime lending rate by 0.125 percentage point to 7.150 percent, effective Thursday.
